text: #810 is dropped, by @gitdek's call on 2026-11-13: the decision follow-up machinery stays where it is, unused. #891, which restored `factory/protocol` to the statements D-0209 ratifies and removed `factory/decision-followup`, is closed without merging, and the decision it carried as proposed was never on main. Restored, the protocol's gate is slower, and its job is CI's longest: 22.4, 25.3 and 28.3 minutes in #891's three runs, against 13.6 to 22.8, median 18.9, over the 46 other pull-request runs from 2026-11-09 to 11-13. Since #428's amendment the model's Next groups its steps as OrdinaryStep and FollowupStep, and the explorer reports each group's distinct outcomes, 1,503,852 over 132,486 states. The earlier model names every step with every argument, and its explorer reports every one it tries, 3,150,750 over 25,206 states. Which of the gate's checks the extra minutes fall in isn't measured, since a receipt doesn't time each check. Merging would have removed 2,617 lines of Go and 1,774 of TLA+ that nothing uses and one CI job of 5 to 7 minutes that no pull request waits for, and changed nothing the factory does. The follow-up statements come out when the protocol is next amended for its own reasons, on the grouped model. On its own, only a measured saving on CI's longest job reopens this.
